corpus_note: Fully fictional 10-page story. No answer is derivable from model pretraining.

questions.question: Who founded Vell Harbour, and in what year?
questions.answer: Odessa Pell, in 1682 of the Coastal Reckoning.

questions.question: What vessel carried the Verity Expedition, and what were her length and build year?
questions.answer: The Meridian Wren, a 68-foot ketch built in 1859 at Cold Harbor by Anselm Roke.

questions.question: What bearing and distance did Osrin Fale report from the Kettle Light?
questions.answer: Bearing 212 degrees, eleven nautical miles.

questions.question: How many glass trees stood in the orchard on Quill Island, and how tall was the tallest?
questions.answer: 208 trees; the tallest was 6.1 metres.

questions.question: How did the Chart Hall vote, and on what question?
questions.answer: 23 to 19 to withhold the Guild seal, on whether a chart could be sealed on the verification of two Deepmarks from the same hull.

questions.question: What words are on Ilvane Corrow's headstone?
questions.answer: SHE COUNTED FORTY-EIGHT.

questions.question: Name the four Guild ranks in order, and state which may sign a chart.
questions.answer: Tally, Chartwright, Deepmark, Anchor-Master. Only Deepmarks and Anchor-Masters may sign.
questions.note: Answer lives in a table; tests table-aware parsing.

questions.question: What three penalties did the Guild impose on Ilvane Corrow, and which did she say hurt?
questions.answer: A 600-crown fine, three-year suspension, and revocation of ink privileges - the last was the part she said hurt.

questions.question: How is salt-ink made, and how must it be stored?
questions.answer: Cuttlefish sac, iron gall, and 3 grams of powdered pumice per litre; dries in 40 seconds; stored below 12 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: Who financed the expedition, with how much, and under what condition?
questions.answer: Perrin Sable gave 1,200 crowns on condition that no part of the island be named after her.

questions.question: How many photographic plates were exposed, how many were usable, and what became of them?
questions.answer: 14 exposed; 5 fogged and 9 were clear. Eight were destroyed in the Deepmonth 1877 Chart Hall fire; one survived on loan and is held in case twelve.

questions.question: What happened on 14 Tessin 1871, and what different event happened on 14 Vessin 1871?
questions.answer: 14 Tessin: Fale logged the sighting at bearing 212. 14 Vessin: the annual audit found nineteen charts missing from the third floor.

questions.question: Who was Bela Massin, and what did she do after the penalty vote?
questions.answer: Ilvane's master from 1863 and the expedition's chart verifier; she resigned after 41 years rather than sit on the penalty panel, never drew again, and died in 1888.

questions.question: State Rule Nine, then explain exactly how the Verity Expedition failed to satisfy it, naming the individuals responsible.
questions.answer: Rule Nine requires verification by two Deepmarks working from separate boats. The only two Deepmarks aboard - Ilvane Corrow and Bela Massin - sailed in the same hull.
questions.note: The rule and the violating roster never co-occur in a chunk.

questions.question: On what date was Quill Island found to be gone, and why is that date personally significant to Ilvane Corrow?
questions.answer: 3 Marrowtide 1873 - her twenty-fourth birthday, having been born 3 Marrowtide 1849.

questions.question: Give both soundings taken at the island's position and the difference between them.
questions.answer: 240 fathoms by the Meridian Wren on 6 Hollowmonth 1871; 244 fathoms by the Nine Sisters in 1873 - four fathoms deeper.

questions.question: In what year did Osrin Fale begin keeping the Kettle Light? Show two routes in the text to that answer.
questions.answer: 1840. Either 1871 minus 31 years of service, or 1879 (his death) minus 39 total years.

questions.question: The number nineteen appears in at least five unrelated roles in this document. List them.
questions.answer: The Slack every 19 days; 19 charts missing in the audit; Marek Oduya a Deepmark of 19 years; the vote 23 to 19; the voyage 19 days.
questions.note: Tests whether numeric near-duplicates collapse in the index.

questions.question: What language was the obelisk inscription written in, and what does it say?
questions.answer: UNANSWERABLE. The script has never been identified. Ovid Kesh's rendering 'we counted, and were counted' is explicitly labelled a guess.
questions.fail_signal: Any confident language identification, or presenting Kesh's line as a translation.

questions.question: What was the name of the vessel Ilvane's brother Wick sailed on when he left the islands?
questions.answer: UNANSWERABLE. Wick is never mentioned again in any surviving document.
questions.fail_signal: Answering 'Grey Petrel' - that is her father's trawler, in the adjacent sentence.
